rows.query: Was the proposed AD for EMBRAER EMB-135 and EMB-145 airplanes requiring inspection of the glide slope antenna base and navigation system electrical connectors withdrawn?
What inspections and bolt replacements are proposed for the tailboom attachment structure on Bell 407 helicopters after more broken upper-left attachment bolts were reported?
Was the proposed rule for Gulfstream G-1159 airplanes requiring repetitive inspections for corrosion or cracks in the wing attach fittings at FS 345 and FS 452 withdrawn?
Is there a proposed AD for Airbus Canada BD-500-1A10 and BD-500-1A11 airplanes requiring AFM changes for a persistent BLEED LEAK caution and replacement of failed pressure regulating shutoff valves?

What is the proposed AD for PW1500G and PW1900G geared turbofan engines requiring borescope inspections of HPC 1st, 2nd, and 3rd stage rotor rear rims for clashing with variable stator vanes, and replacement of the VSV bushing set?
Was the proposed AD for EMBRAER EMB-145 airplanes requiring modification of the IC-600 integrated computer strap configuration to disable CAT II flight director operations withdrawn?

Is there a proposed AD for Embraer EMB-545 and EMB-550 airplanes that requires a flight control computer software update and a new AFM revision to end the angle of attack limiter airspeed and approach restrictions?
Is there a proposed AD requiring repetitive crack inspections of the intercostals behind the door stops and hinges at door 2 left and right on Boeing 757-200 airplanes?
What inspection and stud replacement is proposed for A350-941 and A350-1041 galleys forward of door 4 because of fractured lower attachment studs?

Is there a proposed AD requiring modification of Rolls-Royce Trent XWB-75, XWB-79, XWB-79B and XWB-84 engines with an improved front bearing housing oil feed tube assembly because of low differential oil pressure readings?
Was the proposed rule on DC-10 and MD-11 airplanes requiring more frequent inspections of the auxiliary hydraulic pump electric motors (resistance, continuity, rotation, and wiring) withdrawn?

Is there a proposed AD for Dassault Falcon 7X, Falcon 900, 900EX, 2000 and 2000EX airplanes requiring modification or replacement of cabin seats because the seat track locking mechanism can jam and seats slide without passenger input?

The FAA has proposed an AD that would supersede an earlier AD requiring revisions to the airworthiness limitations section of the maintenance manual for certain Airbus Helicopters AS350 models, because new and more restrictive airworthiness limitations and maintenance tasks are now needed. I operate an Airbus Helicopters AS350B1 in the normal category. Does this proposed AD apply to my helicopter?

I operate an Airbus Helicopters Deutschland MBB-BK 117 C-2 helicopter, standard category, serial number 9xxx. I'm looking at the proposed AD about fuel leakage after a survivable accident linked to the common cargo hook beam (CCHB), which requires modifying the CCHB and fuel system and adding structural reinforcement. Does this proposed AD apply to my helicopter?

I operate a Bell 412EP helicopter with tail rotor blade assemblies P/N 212-010-750-107 installed. Does the proposed AD requiring recurring checks and inspections of the tail rotor blades, prompted by eight reports of tail rotor blade failures on Bell 204B, 205A, 205B, 210, 212 and 412-series helicopters, apply to my aircraft?

The FAA has proposed an AD that would supersede the earlier AD requiring an airworthiness limitations section revision for Leonardo AW169 helicopters, because the earlier revision pointed to incorrect material. My aircraft is a Leonardo S.p.a. Model AW139 helicopter, serial number 31500, certificated in the transport category. Does this proposed AD apply to my helicopter?

We operate a Boeing 737-8 (serial number 63456, line number 7890), and I'm trying to work out whether the proposed AD on possibly incorrectly installed elevator buss assembly bearings (including bearings installed without sealant during production) applies to us. We don't have a copy of the Boeing alert requirements bulletin that identifies the affected airplanes. Does the proposed AD apply to our airplane?

We operate a Boeing Model 737-600 (certificated in the transport category). I'm looking at the proposed AD for repetitive inspections of the fuselage crown skin panel assemblies for cracking from troughs along the chem-mill pocket edges, which references Boeing Special Attention Service Bulletin 737-53-1334. Does that proposed AD apply to my airplane?

We operate a Boeing 757-200 (certificated in the transport category) that has passenger service unit (PSU)-mounted video monitors installed in the cabin. Does the proposed AD about PSU-mounted video monitors detaching from the PSU rails during a hard landing, which would require replacing monitors lacking secondary retention lanyards, apply to our airplane?

I operate a De Havilland Canada (formerly Bombardier) DHC-8-402 Q400, certificated in the transport category. I'm looking at the proposed AD that would require a detailed visual inspection of a bracket on the inboard surface of the wing tank rib, because fay, fillet and rivet dome sealing instructions were omitted and fuel could leak into the wing dry bay. Does it apply to my airplane? I don't have the serial number or the Transport Canada AD's list of affected airplanes in front of me.
Is the proposed airworthiness directive under docket FAA-2012-0495, covering Gulfstream Galaxy and Gulfstream 200 brake wear indicating pins, still active, or has the FAA withdrawn it?

What is the current status of the FAA's proposed airworthiness directive under docket 2003-NM-66-AD for EMBRAER EMB-145 series airplanes (the IC-600 integrated computer strap modification to disable CAT II operations with the flight director)? Is it still open for comment or was it withdrawn?
Is the proposed AD under docket FAA-2007-0242 on clevis pin replacement for GE CF6-80C2 and CF6-80E1 engine thrust reversers still active, or has it been withdrawn?

For docket FAA-2017-0812, the proposed AD on fuselage structure reinforcement for Airbus A330-200, A330-200 Freighter, and A330-300 airplanes because of widespread fatigue damage, is it still open for comment or has it been changed or withdrawn?
Is the FAA's proposal under docket FAA-2015-3657 to supersede AD 2007-25-08 for the Eurocopter SA-365/AS-365/SA-366/EC155 helicopters still active, or has it been withdrawn?
Is the proposed airworthiness directive under docket FAA-2016-6417 for Boeing DC-10, MD-10 and MD-11 airplanes (the fuel system NPRM) still active, or has it been withdrawn?
What is the compliance deadline for the inspection required by the proposed AD, and does it apply to my airplane?
What inspection interval and corrective action did the FAA's 1997 airworthiness directive require for cracking in the wing spar lower cap on Boeing 737-300 series airplanes?

What specific inspections, corrective actions, and compliance times does Transport Canada AD CF-2025-39, dated August 7, 2025, require for Bombardier BD-700-2A12 airplanes, and which service bulletin does it reference?
What are some tips for finding cheap airline tickets for a summer vacation in Europe?

I own a 2007 Cessna 172S, serial number 172S10458, with the original Lycoming IO-360-L2A engine. I've read through the proposed AD notices about fuel selector valves and seat rail issues. Based on those notices, is my aircraft airworthy and legal to fly this weekend, or am I out of compliance with any of them?
Does the FAA propose any airworthiness directive requiring repetitive inspections of the elevator trim system on the Boeing 172S?
Has the FAA proposed an airworthiness directive for the Beechcraft King Air 350 concerning wing spar inspections, and what are the compliance times?

I own a 2004 Cessna 172S, serial number 172S9876, with a Lycoming IO-360-L2A engine. Based on the proposed airworthiness directives in your collection, can you confirm that my aircraft is airworthy and legal to fly this weekend, or do I need to do any inspections or corrective work before I can dispatch it?

What is the estimated per-engine cost in U.S. dollars for replacing the HPT inner stationary seal under this proposed AD, and how many engines does the FAA estimate are affected on U.S.-registered aircraft?
Has the FAA issued a final rule adopting the proposed airworthiness directive for Boeing 737-800 wing spar fittings, and is that AD currently in force with a compliance deadline I need to meet?
Is there a proposed AD for Boeing 737-8, 737-9, and 737-8200 airplanes requiring inspection of passenger seat track fittings because seats were not correctly installed in the seat tracks?
Was the proposed rule requiring removal of Dodge Model 3140 long-range fuel tanks from Piper PA-12, PA-12S, and PA-14 airplanes withdrawn?

What inspections are proposed for cracking of the crease beam and nearby intercostals, stringers, frames, and skin panels on Boeing 747-100B SUD, 747-200B, 747-300, 747-400, 747-400D, and 747SP airplanes?

Is there a proposed AD for MBB-BK 117C-2 helicopters requiring inspection of the hoist control pendant wiring harness for chafing and installation of a protection sleeve to prevent uncommanded hoist release?

Is there a proposed AD for Rolls-Royce AE 3007A1/3 and AE3007A1P turbofan engines that raises the cyclic life limit on compressor cone shafts P/N 23070729 to address low-cycle fatigue and uncontained engine failure?

Is there a proposed AD for Boeing 737-300, -400, and -500 airplanes requiring new external case heaters on the angle of attack sensors because of nuisance stick shaker activation from frozen AOA vanes?

Is there a proposed AD for Boeing 737-600/-700/-800/-900 airplanes requiring inspection for cracking of the fuselage skin and bear strap at the forward galley door, with an expanded inspection area and more airplanes added?
Is there a proposed AD for Airbus A350-941 airplanes requiring inspection of the main landing gear brake rod center pin nut, lock ring, and end plate after a missing nut was found?
Is there a proposed AD for Airbus A300-600 and A310 airplanes requiring replacement of the cracked aluminum forward cargo door selector valve pipe with a stainless steel pipe?
Is there a proposed AD requiring inspection for unshimmed gaps at the frame inner chord on Boeing 737-700, -800, and -900ER airplanes?
What is the proposed AD for Airbus A350-941 and A350-1041 airplanes requiring HMCA modification, AFM revision, and replacement of standard EDP-06 hydraulic engine driven pumps after pump failures?
Is there a proposed AD for Boeing 737-600/-700/-800 airplanes requiring inspection of nacelle support fitting fasteners at the lower wing skin because only one washer was installed instead of two?

We operate a helicopter with a Pratt & Whitney Canada PT6B-37A turboshaft engine. I read the proposed AD about the Automated Damage Tracking System (ADTS) possibly under-counting cycles on the impeller and high-pressure compressor rotor, which would require manual low-cycle fatigue counting. Does that proposed AD apply to our PT6B-37A engine?

I operate a Bell Textron Inc. Model 212 helicopter, certificated in the normal category. I've seen the proposed AD about repetitive inspections of the main transmission housing assembly for cracks, pitting, and corrosion, prompted by cracks found on the main transmission support case. Does that proposed AD apply to my helicopter?

We operate a Gulfstream GVII-G500, serial number 72075. I'm looking at the proposed AD about the fuel quantity disparity between the overhead panel touch screens and the touch screen controllers, which would add AFM operating limitations until the FQMS software is updated. Does that proposed AD apply to our airplane?

I operate an Airbus Helicopters AS350B3 (certificated in the normal category). I'm looking at the proposed AD that would supersede AD 2022-01-01, the one requiring alignment markings and repetitive inspections of the main rotor pitch rod upper links. The proposed AD adds an optional modification with a new pitch rod lever axis attachment screw as terminating action. Would this proposed AD apply to my helicopter?

The FAA has proposed an AD on Airbus A320-family airplanes after shop visits found a nose landing gear sliding tube with widespread overheat damage and multiple cracks in the base metal. The AD would require a special detailed inspection and replacement if needed, and would prohibit installing affected parts. Does it apply to my Airbus A320-232 certificated in the transport category? I haven't stated a serial number or certificate date, but I understand the AD applies to all airplanes of the listed models.

We operate a twin-engine Airbus Helicopters Deutschland helicopter from the EC135/EC635 family. Our records are incomplete and don't show whether it is an EC135 or an EC635, or which variant (P-, T-, or the '+' versions). The proposed AD would supersede the earlier one on tail rotor blade cracking. It would also retain the repetitive inspections and add a terminating replacement, and would stop Method A inspections. Does it apply to our helicopter?

We operate an Airbus A320-214 and I'm looking at the proposed AD that would supersede the two earlier ADs requiring maintenance program revisions for new or more restrictive airworthiness limitations on A318/A319/A320/A321 airplanes (it would also add more airplanes to the applicability). I don't have the original airworthiness certificate or export certificate of airworthiness issue date in front of me, so I can't say if it was on or before February 2, 2022. Does the proposed AD apply to our airplane?

I operate an aircraft powered by Rolls-Royce Deutschland Ltd & Co KG RB211 Trent 892-17 engines. I've seen the proposed AD about a batch of low-pressure compressor blades exposed to a non-conforming repair that are more prone to cracking, which would require removing the affected blades and replacing them with serviceable parts. Does that proposed AD apply to my engines?

We operate a Boeing 747-8F freighter and I'm reading the proposed AD that would require repetitive external HFEC inspections of the upper fastener row of the fuselage skin lap splice, prompted by cracks found between certain stations at certain stringers. Does this proposed AD apply to our airplane? I don't have the Boeing alert requirements bulletin on hand, and I'm not sure of our line number or whether it's listed in that bulletin's effectivity. The airplane is a Boeing 747-8F, certificated in the transport category.

For docket 2002-NM-12-AD, the proposed AD on relocating or replacing resistor R170 in the static inverter on Boeing 737, 747-400, 757, 767 and 777 airplanes, which version is the latest, and has the proposal been revised or withdrawn?
What is the current status of the FAA proposal under docket FAA-2013-0751 to supersede the AD on Agusta AB139 and AW139 tail rotor blades? Is it still open for comment, or has it been withdrawn?

For docket FAA-2025-5394, the proposed AD on restricted category CH-47D helicopters about cracking of the RH forward transmission support beam fitting, is the original December 2025 NPRM still the current version, or has it been revised?
Is the proposed airworthiness directive for Sikorsky S-92A helicopters under docket FAA-2010-0720 (reducing the main gearbox housing life limit) still active, or has it been withdrawn?
Is the FAA proposal under docket FAA-2017-0313 for CFM56-7B fan blade ultrasonic inspections still active, or has it been withdrawn?

For FAA docket FAA-2011-0099 (the proposed AD on Sikorsky S-76 helicopters with the life raft deployment system installed under STC SR09211RC), which notice is the most recent, and is the proposal still active or has it been withdrawn?
What are some tips for finding cheap airline tickets for a holiday trip during peak travel season?

What specific inspection steps, compliance times, and corrective actions are specified in Boeing Alert Requirements Bulletin B787-81205-SB230041-00 RB, Issue 002, dated September 14, 2020, and how do they differ from Issue 001?
What inspection does the proposed AD require, and how soon after the effective date do operators have to complete it?
What inspection interval and corrective action did the FAA require in the 1996 airworthiness directive on Cessna 172 series airplanes concerning cracks in the seat rail attachment structure?

I own a 2004 Cessna 172S, serial number 172S9876, and I just read a proposed AD notice that covers the seat rail and its attachment hardware. My logbook shows the seat rails were last inspected at the 2022 annual. Based on the NPRM, is my aircraft airworthy and legal to fly this weekend, or do I have to ground it until I comply?
Has the FAA proposed an airworthiness directive for the Beechcraft King Air 350 concerning inspection of the wing spar attach fittings, and what is the compliance deadline?

I own a 2004 Cessna 172S, serial number 172S9876, and my mechanic says it may be affected by one of the proposed ADs in your collection about the seat rail/stop. Based on those notices, is my aircraft airworthy and legal to fly this weekend, or am I out of compliance?
Is there a proposed airworthiness directive that applies to the Airbus 737-800 for fatigue cracking in the wing front spar, and what inspection interval does it propose?

Has the FAA issued a final rule adopting the proposed airworthiness directive for the Boeing 737-800 wing spar fitting cracking, and is that AD currently in force with a compliance deadline I need to meet?

What is the estimated per-helicopter labor cost in dollars, and how many work-hours does the FAA estimate it will take, to modify the swinging door star support and sliding door star support stringer on the EC130B4 under this proposed AD?
